newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Acer Peripherals up sharply late trade.
newsitem.headline: Acer Peripherals up sharply late trade.

text.p: Taiwan's Acer Peripherals rose sharply in late trade on Monday after the company announced it had averted an import ban threatened by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, brokers said.
With 45 minutes left, Acer Peripherals was up 3.77 percent or T$1.70 to T$46.80.

Acer Peripherals, a key member of Acer Group and the world's third largest computer monitor maker, said the FDA had decided not to impose an import ban on the company after determining it had complied with U.S. quality-control requirements.

The FDA had threatened Acer Peripherals with a ban after citing the firm for failing to provide adequate assurances that monitors produced at its Taoyuan plant did not emit prohibited levels of radiation.
Acer Peripherals has consistently denied that its monitors were dangerous, saying the discrepancy was over methods of testing and reporting, not the quality of its products.
"The news of FDA not issuing a ban is obviously good for Acer Peripherals and one that boosts investor confidence in the company," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment.
